newsitem.title: USA: Albright, Qian upbeat about China WTO prospects.
newsitem.headline: Albright, Qian upbeat about China WTO prospects.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen were upbeat Monday about prospects for agreement on China's entry into the World Trade Organization, perhaps before a Sino-U.S. summit later this year.

"We are very hopeful that progress on these discussions will in fact be fruitful," Albright told reporters when asked if negotiations could be completed before a planned summit between Presidents Bill Clinton and Jiang Zemin.
Qian, at a news conference at the start of talks with Albright, said recent negotiations had been positive, though the issues were complicated.
"Both China and the United States share the commmon aspiration to resolve the question as soon as possible...I believe that as time goes by these questions will be resolved," he said.
Albright and Qian were meeting to prepare the way for the summit, whose date and U.S. location have yet to be announced. It is to be followed by a visit by Clinton to China in 1998.

On Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade benefits for China -- which some congressmen would like to withhold -- Albright said: "We believe it is very important for the MFN to go forwards...It is a strategic imperative for this (U.S.-China) relationship to go forward and the trade relationship is very important in that regard."
